newsitem.title: USA: Dupont reports record second-quarter earnings.
newsitem.headline: Dupont reports record second-quarter earnings.

text.p: Chemical giant DuPont Co. on Wednesday reported record second-quarter profits, a 14 percent jump fuelled by growth in its chemicals and specialities business and continued strength in its petroleum operations.

Net income hit $1.14 billion, or $1.01 per share, in the quarter ended June 30, compared with $1 billion, or 89 cents a share, in last year's second quarter. Per-share results reflected a 2-for-1 stock split that took effect May 15.
The earnings by one of the nation's biggest chemical companies were in line with analysts' expectations, according to market research firm First Call.
Sales totalled $11.4 billion for the quarter, a 2 percent increase from $11.1 billion a year ago.
DuPont's stock rose 81 cents to $67 in consolidated late morning New York Stock Exchange trading.

The Wilmington, Del.-based company, known for developing products like nylon and spandex, said the quarter's results reflected record earnings by its fibers and polymers units, combined with continued strong performance by its Conoco petroleum unit, particularly in refining and marketing.
DuPont said its agricultural products business also had a strong quarter and was a key contributor to growth in chemicals and specialities.
For the first half of 1997, DuPont earned $2.2 billion, or $1.91 a share, compared with $1.9 billion, or $1.68 a share, last year.

"We are well on our way to a fourth consecutive year of record earnings," DuPont President John Krol said in a statement. "Total return to DuPont shareholders was 36 percent for the first half of this year, exceeding industry averages."

Second-quarter earnings from fibers increased 18 percent to $245 million from $208 million in the year-ago period, mainly due to increased earnings from its Lycra brand of spandex and Dacron polyester.
Petroleum earned $246 million, a second-quarter record and a 13 percent increase from $218 million last year. Polymers made $259 million, up 6 percent from $244 million in 1996.
Earnings from chemicals slipped 17 percent to $137 million from $165 million in the year-ago period.
DuPont said higher sales of its chemicals and specialities were offset by lower prices outside the United States, largely due to the stronger dollar.
